title: mcp: the stdio record resource objectstack://objects/{name}/records/{id} answers a missing or hidden id as an uncoded { error }, while its own refusals and the get_record tool answer RECORD_NOT_FOUND 404
body:
epic:#32897#1 · os-tesla · session_01L9qibzoApSyVPuia3NCrBY

Filing gate: ① a named-site behaviour gap, class b. Carried out of #33030 (PR #33175, head `59ccee50`): the card thread's out-of-scope finding (1), re-read by the seat at that head. ⛔ Not a claim; triage sets the lane and grade.
reach: the stdio MCP resource template `objectstack://objects/{objectName}/records/{recordId}` (`packages/mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.ts` ~:2122–2142 at PR #33175's head). Read from code and measured by the card thread at that head; not measured on a deployment.

## Business reason

After PR #33175, a stdio client that asks the `get_record` tool for a missing or hidden id gets the coded `{ error: { code: "RECORD_NOT_FOUND", status: 404 } }` the HTTP door answers. The same client reading the record **resource** for the same id still gets `{"error":"Record \"<id>\" not found in \"<object>\""}` with no `code` and no `status`, although every thrown refusal on that resource (its `catch`, #23509 / #31270) already answers `{ error, code, status }`. A client that branches on the code must special-case the resource's miss.

## What is true at PR #33175's head

- The resource's `if (!record)` branch writes `JSON.stringify({ error: ... })` only.
- Its `catch` renders `dataDoorRefusalEnvelope(err, objectName)` with `code` and `status`.
- `get_record` now throws `recordNotFoundError(objectName, recordId)` (`@objectstack/core`) into its own catch for a null read.

## Expected

The record resource answers a missing or hidden id with the same `{ error, code: "RECORD_NOT_FOUND", status: 404 }` members its other refusals carry, identical for missing and hidden ids (no existence oracle). `error` stays a string.

Dedupe: `is:issue is:open stdio record resource not found code` → #33030 (the tool half, PR #33175), #33156; none for the resource.

Part of the MCP epic #32897 (M3: answers that agree with the gate).
